claims.text: A compound sparse index made solely of ascending/descending fields includes a document when at least one indexed field exists. Do not assume {tenant: 1, optional: 1} with sparse: true excludes every document missing optional; an explicit partial existence filter expresses that requirement. (medium confidence)

If the intended result excludes both missing fields and explicit nulls, $ne:null expresses that requirement; it is not a semantics-preserving replacement for $exists:true when null-valued fields must match. (low confidence)

Use explain execution statistics to verify the intended partial-index plan and document retrieval costs. Logical membership equivalence between sparse and partial indexes does not establish identical covered-query behavior: SERVER-26896 records a requested planner improvement for covering an exists predicate from a partial filter. (medium confidence)

MongoDB normally uses a partial index only when the query condition implies its filter or a narrower subset. A query omitting the existence requirement, or asking for missing fields, cannot safely use an existence-filtered partial index if matching documents lie outside it. Eligibility does not guarantee selection. (high confidence)

A sparse index on field f cannot correctly answer {f:{$exists:false}}, because its entries omit the matching documents. MongoDB documents COLLSCAN for that sparse-index case, while a non-sparse index requires FETCH; additional predicates or indexes can change the overall query plan. (high confidence)

partialFilterExpression supports $exists: true, but $exists: false is rejected. LibreChat reported an index-build failure with Expression not supported in partial index: $not; Mongoose maintainers separately documented this restriction in MongoDB 3.2. (medium confidence)
The sparse option and partialFilterExpression cannot be specified together on one index; choose the membership mechanism appropriate to the query. (medium confidence)

For a single-field sparse index, documents with the field are indexed, including explicit null values; documents missing the field are omitted. Consequently, $exists: true includes null and must not be treated as a non-null predicate. (high confidence)

For a single field, createIndex({f:1},{partialFilterExpression:{f:{$exists:true}}}) expresses the sparse membership rule. Partial indexes also allow filters on fields outside the index key, enabling finer selection than sparse indexes. (high confidence)

For the indexed-field $exists: true predicate, MongoDB documents an exact sparse-index match without a FETCH to establish existence, whereas a non-sparse index requires FETCH. Returning full documents can still require document retrieval; predicate evaluation alone does not establish that the whole query is covered. (medium confidence)

Do not force a sparse index for an unfiltered count or a sort that must include documents missing its key. MongoDB normally avoids this incomplete result, but an explicit sparse-index hint can return only the indexed subset and produce an incorrect all-document count. (medium confidence)

LibreChat issue 16031 reports that a missing-field partial filter prevented its cleanup index from building on each startup, while the cleanup query continued without that index. The report names LibreChat v0.8.8-rc3 and MongoDB 8.3.7; these are reporter-provided versions, not reproduced measurements. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-16)

The current partialFilterExpression operator list supports $exists:true, not $exists:false; arbitrary query predicates are not valid partial filters. MongoDB also prohibits combining sparse and partialFilterExpression on the same index. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

AWS examples must be scoped to Amazon DocumentDB and its planner. Its older indexing article requires explicit $exists for sparse-index selection; the November 11, 2025 new-planner article demonstrates planner version 2 using an existence-filtered index for non-null equality without explicit $exists. These are not MongoDB planner requirements. (high confidence) (verified as of 2025-11-11)
